{{Recipe}}

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Liter|L]] (8 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]) red [[Cookbook:Wine|wine]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Peach|peaches]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Apple|apple]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Banana|banana]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Orange|orange]]
*3 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemons]]
*125 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (¼ cup) [[Cookbook:Brandy|brandy]]
*4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] stick (optional)
==Procedure==
#Pour the wine in a container large enough to hold all the ingredients.
#Add the lemon juice, orange and lemon segments, apple pieces, and banana slices.
#Add sugar and brandy; stir to mix well using a wooden spoon. Add cinnamon.
#Keep in the fridge for at least an hour. Add ice cubes and let it stand 10 minutes before serving.
#Serve in tall glasses, including fruit bits.

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*The longer the fruit is [[Cookbook:Macerating|macerating]] in the wine, the better the taste (up to 24 hours total). In that case, add the banana slices ½–1 hour before serving to prevent them from getting too soft.
*You can use any kind of fruit you like. Try other liqueurs instead of brandy.
*For a sweeter version, add ½–1 L (2–4 cups) [[Cookbook:Lemonade|lemonade]] instead of the lemon juice.
*Don’t forget a spoon to eat the fruit once finished with sangría.
